item.title: [Yahoo Sports] 2026 MLB Playoffs: ALDS, NLDS predictions and World Series picks
item.dc:creator: Rotoworld Staff
item.description: With the Wild Card round of the 2026 MLB Playoffs behind us, it's time for the Division Series to get underway. It all starts on Saturday with all four Division Series matchups. With that in mind, we polled the Rotoworld Baseball staff for their thoughts on how the rest of the postseason will play out. Check out our picks and analysis for the Division Series, Championship Series, and World Series. The 2026 MLB postseason has arrived. Stay up to date with the latest results and more. 2026 ALDS, N
item.content:encoded:
With the Wild Card round of the 2026 MLB Playoffs behind us, it's time for the Division Series to get underway. It all starts on Saturday with all four Division Series matchups.
With that in mind, we polled the Rotoworld Baseball staff for their thoughts on how the rest of the postseason will play out. Check out our picks and analysis for the Division Series, Championship Series, and World Series.
The 2026 MLB postseason has arrived. Stay up to date with the latest results and more.
2026 ALDS, NLDS Predictions
| Writer | White Sox vs. Guardians | Yankees vs. Rays | Braves vs. Dodgers | Padres vs. Brewers |
| Eric Samulski | Guardians | Yankees | Dodgers | Brewers |
| Matthew Pouliot | Guardians | Yankees | Dodgers | Brewers |
| David Shovein | Guardians | Rays | Dodgers | Brewers |
| Christopher Crawford | White Sox | Yankees | Dodgers | Padres |
| D.J. Short | Guardians | Yankees | Dodgers | Padres |
White Sox vs. Guardians
Crawford: I don't think there's much of a difference between the White Sox and the Guardians. I think the fact that the White Sox already won a pair of postseason games on the road, both relatively convincingly, is something working in their favor. I can't quite go team of destiny or any of that stuff, but there does seem to be something about this White Sox team. I realize that's not exactly the most scientific answer, but my heart believes in the Chicago Popes.
Yankees vs. Rays
Short: The Rays and Yankees are set to meet in the postseason for the second time ever, and the first with actual fans in the building. While the Rays were the better regular season team this year, I think the Yankees are better built for the postseason. It starts with the rotation, which was the best in the majors with a 3.30 ERA, but their bullpen was even better with a 3.15 ERA. Drew Rasmussen has dominated the Yankees in his career, but New York has a level of rotation depth the Rays simply can't match.
Aaron Judge's status for the ALDS remains uncertain because of his calf injury, but even without him, one could argue that the Yankees have the more dangerous lineup. Their ability to change the game with one swing is something I think will win out over Tampa Bay's small-ball style in a short series.
Braves vs. Dodgers
Pouliot: Atlanta's pitching staff received 7 2/3 innings from Chris Sale and seven from Tyler Mahle and still seemed hard-pressed to get through the three-game Wild Card series against the Phillies. How are they going to hold up without those two to start the series against the Dodgers? Even without the relief appearance Thursday, starting Sale in Game 2 would have required pitching him on four days' rest, which he hasn't done since early April. As is, it looks like Sale in Game 3 and Mahle in Game 4. Maybe the Dodgers' bats start off cold and the Braves can steal a game in Los Angeles, but as shorthanded as they are in terms of pitching depth, not having their rotation lined puts them at a major disadvantage.
Padres vs. Brewers
Samulski: The Padres have been red hot and dominated the Cubs, but I published an article before the postseason with research from the last 10 years that showed teams coming into the playoffs with tons of momentum don't meaningfully perform better than teams who struggle coming into the postseason. I might as well trust my own research. The Brewers have been arguably the best team in baseball all season. Their lineup is incredibly tough to get out, and they have possibly the deepest overall pitching staff in the postseason.
Full MLB Postseason Predictions
| Writer | ALCS Winner | NLCS Winner | World Series Champion |
| Eric Samulski | New York Yankees | Milwaukee Brewers | Milwaukee Brewers |
| Matthew Pouliot | New York Yankees | Los Angeles Dodgers | Los Angeles Dodgers |
| David Shovein | Tampa Bay Rays | Milwaukee Brewers | Tampa Bay Rays |
| Christopher Crawford | New York Yankees | San Diego Padres | San Diego Padres |
| D.J. Short | New York Yankees | San Diego Padres | New York Yankees |
Samulski: I will admit my bias again when talking about why I picked against the Yankees. I just think this Brewers team is finally going to break through. The Yankees were lights out against the Red Sox, but they have been prone to strikeouts throughout the season. That can make them a volatile offense, and I think the consistency of the Brewers will win the day here.
Pouliot: A few weeks ago, I might have picked another champ, but with the Dodgers' bullpen rounding into form, their biggest potential weakness seems gone. Edwin Díaz still isn't a sure thing, but he was much improved after coming off the IL, allowing just one hit and one walk while striking out nine in his final five innings. Roki Sasaki and Evan Phillips both hit 100 mph last week, and Kris Bubic, if he's even needed, could prove to be a secret weapon. Shohei Ohtani and Freddie Freeman might not be able to carry the offense at this point, but even if the Dodgers are lacking their usual firepower, they should be able to win some low-scoring games.
Crawford: I don't think the Padres are the best team in baseball. I don't think they're even the best team in their division. But I love the way they're playing now, and that bullpen, quality starters at the top of the rotation and just enough star power makes me believe they're built for the postseason, and their first-ever World Series championship.
Short: I love the Yankees' pitching and Aaron Judge should be back eventually in some capacity, which only improves the team's outlook for a potential World Series matchup. As opposed to their meeting in 1998, I would expect the Padres to make this one much more competitive. San Diego's offense has been great in the second half and their bullpen is positively scary. Still, the Yankees would hold the major edge in starting pitching, and that would ultimately make the difference in my hypothetical World Series matchup.

item.title: [MLB.com] Braves-Dodgers NLDS Game 1 FAQ (4 p.m. ET, FOX/FOX One)
item.dc:creator: Sonja Chen; Mark Bowman
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- The last time the Braves and Dodgers met in the postseason, a trip to the World Series was on the line. The Braves ousted the Dodgers in the 2021 NL Championship Series, going on to win the fourth championship in franchise history. But since then, Atlanta has not made it past the Division Series round, while L.A. is the defending back-to-back champion. The Dodgers' three-peat bid will begin in earnest when they take on the Braves in the 2026 NL Division Series starting this Saturd
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- The last time the Braves and Dodgers met in the postseason, a trip to the World Series was on the line.
The Braves ousted the Dodgers in the 2021 NL Championship Series, going on to win the fourth championship in franchise history. But since then, Atlanta has not made it past the Division Series round, while L.A. is the defending back-to-back champion.
The Dodgers' three-peat bid will begin in earnest when they take on the Braves in the 2026 NL Division Series starting this Saturday afternoon at Dodger Stadium, with triple-digit heat in the forecast.
During the regular season, the Braves outplayed the Dodgers, winning five of their six meetings and outscoring them 26-15. But the postseason is a different beast, and a rested L.A. club will meet an Atlanta team that had to play hard to eliminate Philadelphia from the best-of-three Wild Card Series.
When is the game and how can I watch it?
First pitch for Game 1 is set for 4 p.m. ET/1 p.m. PT on Saturday at Dodger Stadium. It will be broadcast on FOX, FOX Deportes and FOX ONE.
Who are the starting pitchers?
Braves: TBD
Injuries have depleted Atlanta's rotation. Chris Sale won’t be available before Game 2 on Sunday, and Tyler Mahle won’t be available before Game 3 on Tuesday. As for Martín Pérez, who was placed on the injured list with low back inflammation on Sept. 1, he couldn’t be activated before Game 3. Grant Holmes threw just two innings in Thursday’s win over the Phillies, so he may be asked to pitch the first few innings. Or, the Braves could go with Brent Suter as an opener and have Holmes follow.
Yamamoto had already established himself as a big-game pitcher long before arriving in the Majors, but he took it to another level last postseason when he tossed consecutive complete games in the NLCS and the World Series before closing out the winner-take-all Game 7 on zero days' rest. Yamamoto taking the ball in Game 1 would be the only way to have him available for a potential Game 5 on his usual rest.
What might the starting lineups look like?
Braves: Michael Harris II, Matt Olson and Drake Baldwin will have to contend with a lefty in Skubal again after facing two left-handed starters in Jesús Luzardo and Cristopher Sánchez during the Wild Card Series.
Dodgers: After Shohei Ohtani recovered from right biceps and left knee injuries and returned from the 15-day IL, manager Dave Roberts began using a platoon in the leadoff spot, slotting in Ohtani against right-handers and Mookie Betts against left-handers. The leadoff platoon, as well as other tweaks corresponding to the handedness of the opposing starter, is expected to continue in the postseason.
How will the bullpens line up after the starter?
Braves: Didier Fuentes might be the only reliever who isn’t available. He pitched three consecutive days during the Wild Card Series. Robert Suarez has surrendered an extra-base hit in each of the three appearances he’s had since his right elbow inflammation forced him to the injured list in June. But his velocity was up and he looked more like himself while throwing two-thirds of an inning Thursday. He’ll likely get some high-leverage spots, especially with Dylan Lee struggling most of the second half and into the postseason.
Dodgers: L.A. may not have a set closer this postseason, but Tanner Scott, Roki Sasaki and Edwin Díaz all seem to be viable ninth-inning options. Righty reliever Edgardo Henriquez, whose regular season ended early due to a lower back strain, is expected to be activated for the NLDS as long as he comes out of bye week workouts feeling good, bolstering the Dodgers' already solid mix of leverage arms.
Any injuries of note?
Dodgers: Of the players who ended the season on the IL, the Dodgers are most confident about Henriquez returning. World Series hero Will Klein (right elbow discomfort) has faced hitters, but he has not pitched in a game since July 31 and is viewed as more of a depth option.
Who is hot and who is not?
Braves: Olson, Albies and Harris all homered in Thursday’s win over the Phillies. Harris went 5-for-11 in the Wild Card Series. Baldwin went 2-for-13 and Acuña was 1-for-9.
Dodgers: In September, Betts (1.112 OPS) and Teoscar Hernández (.965 OPS) were two of the Dodgers' hottest hitters. Tucker (.890 OPS) had his best month by far in his disappointing first season in L.A., perhaps getting hot at the right time.
Freeman dealt with right patellar tendinitis early last month, and he has slugged just .355 since the beginning of July. Ohtani recorded a .666 OPS in his past 29 games, when his biceps and knee injuries flared up and impacted his performance.
Anything else fans might want to know?
• The Dodgers are bidding for the fifth three-peat in World Series history, and the first since the 1998-2000 Yankees. They would be the first National League team to pull off the feat.
• The Braves and Dodgers will be meeting in the postseason for the sixth time. Atlanta was victorious in the 1996 NLDS and the 2021 NLCS. Los Angeles won the 2013 NLDS, 2018 NLDS and 2020 NLCS.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] What WAR Tells Us about the Dodgers' Postseason Prospects
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA — The Dodgers’ roster gives opposing managers plenty to worry about, and WAR helps explain why. It also gives Dodger fans a reason to appreciate players whose contributions can get overshadowed by the biggest names on the marquee. Put hitting, pitching, defense and baserunning on a common scale, and the picture becomes more interesting than a collection of home run totals and earned run averages. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — The Dodgers’ roster gives opposing managers plenty to worry about, and WAR helps explain why. It also gives Dodger fans a reason to appreciate players whose contributions can get overshadowed by the biggest names on the marquee. Put hitting, pitching, defense and baserunning on a common scale, and the picture becomes more interesting than a collection of home run totals and earned run averages.
MLB’s projected playoff rosters rank Milwaukee first (53.7 WAR), Los Angeles second (52.0); Dodgers free-agent acquisitions account for 24.5. That makes for an intriguing October argument: how much should we trust the accumulated value of a roster when the season becomes a succession of short series?
First, it helps to understand what the number actually means.
WAR stands for Wins Above Replacement. It estimates how many additional wins a player contributes compared with a readily available replacement, such as a minor league free agent. A four-WAR player has provided roughly four wins beyond that baseline over his playing time. The comparison uses a standardized replacement level, rather than whoever happens to be sitting on his team’s bench.
For position players, FanGraphs combines batting, baserunning and fielding contributions, expressed in runs. It adjusts for position, league and ballpark, incorporates the replacement-level baseline, and converts those runs into wins. Roughly speaking, about 10 additional runs are worth one win, although the conversion varies with the scoring environment. Position matters because filling a demanding defensive assignment carries value that a batting line alone cannot capture.
Pitchers require a different calculation. FanGraphs starts with Fielding Independent Pitching, emphasizing strikeouts, walks, hit batters and home runs, with an adjustment for infield flies. It accounts for ballpark, innings and the different roles of starters and relievers, then converts performance above replacement into wins. Relievers also receive a leverage adjustment reflecting the situations in which they pitch. Consequently, a pitcher’s ERA and his WAR can tell somewhat different stories.
These are FanGraphs figures, commonly called fWAR. Baseball-Reference uses a different calculation, particularly for pitchers, so its totals can differ. WAR is also an estimate: a few tenths of a win should never end an argument about which player is better.
Here are the Dodgers’ leading contributors on the FanGraphs leaderboard:
| Player | 2026 Dodgers WAR |
|---|---|
| Shohei Ohtani | 6.6 |
| Yoshinobu Yamamoto | 4.7 |
| Andy Pages | 4.5 |
| Max Muncy | 4.2 |
| Mookie Betts | 3.7 |
| Freddie Freeman | 2.7 |
| Tanner Scott | 2.4 |
| Tyler Glasnow | 2.4 |
| Tarik Skubal | 2.2 |
| Justin Wrobleski | 1.9 |
| Blake Snell | 1.9 |
FanGraphs figures through the regular season, accessed September 29. Skubal’s entry reflects his Dodgers work.
Ohtani’s total combines 3.7 WAR as a position player with 2.9 on the mound. Yamamoto supplied his value across 185 innings. Pages and Muncy both cleared four wins, an excellent reminder to give them their share of the credit. Scott’s placement alongside Glasnow is striking, too, given how much less opportunity relievers generally have to accumulate value.
For October, the workload details deserve attention: Glasnow accumulated his total in 74 innings, Snell in 42⅔ and Skubal in 62 for Los Angeles. Their season totals describe what they contributed over those opportunities; a postseason rotation presents a different distribution of innings.
That is where I find the strongest argument for the Dodgers. A playoff team can concentrate its innings among its best available pitchers. If those arms are healthy and effective, the version of a club taking the field in October can be considerably more dangerous than its season-long totals suggest. The same principle works in reverse when an important contributor is unavailable.
I would take the Dodgers’ combination of options into any series with confidence. Having several plausible game-changers gives a manager room to respond when an opponent neutralizes one part of the roster. It also gives the lineup a chance to survive a quiet series from a star.
Still, picking Los Angeles over any individual opponent is a different proposition from picking it over the entire field. Every additional round creates another opportunity for a brilliant opposing starter, a costly mistake or a badly timed slump to decide things. WAR can help establish expectations; October still gets to write the results.
For Dodger fans, these numbers support optimism and an appreciation of how many players have helped put the club in this position. The roster has enough talent to make a championship a reasonable expectation. Turning that expectation into another parade remains the most difficult part.
More Dodgers Coverage:
Have you subscribed to the Bleed Los Podcast YouTube channel? Be sure to ring the notification bell to watch player interviews, participate in shows & promotions, and stay up to date on all Dodgers news and rumors!
A lifelong baseball fan, Webb has been going to Dodger games since he moved to Los Angeles in 1987. His favorite memory was attending the insane Game 3 of the World Series in 2025 and hugging random Dodgers fans after Freddie’s walkoff homer. He has been writing for Dodgersbeat since 2020.

item.title: [MLB.com] Forever connected by Braves, Olson and Freeman welcome first postseason faceoff
item.dc:creator: Mark Bowman
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- Freddie Freeman’s assumption that he would spend his entire career with Atlanta ended on March 14, 2022, the day the Braves acquired Matt Olson from the A’s. It was an awkward and initially painful separation for the man who had been the Braves’ everyday first baseman from 2011-2021. But over this next
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- Freddie Freeman’s assumption that he would spend his entire career with Atlanta ended on March 14, 2022, the day the Braves acquired Matt Olson from the A’s. It was an awkward and initially painful separation for the man who had been the Braves’ everyday first baseman from 2011-2021.
Needless to say, the pain has faded as Freeman has spent the past five years establishing himself as a legend in another organization. He’ll always cherish his days with the Braves. But over this next week, they will stand as the enemy.
Freeman’s Dodgers will face the Braves in the National League Division Series that begins on Saturday at Dodger Stadium. The 2020 NL MVP has played 29 games against Atlanta over the past five seasons. But this marks the first time he will face his original organization in the postseason.
“I understand it will be a storyline,” Freeman said. “I get it. But it is five years later. I'm not going to try and look at it any differently. It's another team that I'm trying to get through to win another championship.”
The NLDS will create another opportunity to highlight the link that will forever exist between Freeman and Olson, the two players who have combined to provide the Braves excellence at first base over the past two decades.
Freeman certainly didn’t like seeing his job given to somebody else. As for Olson, it wasn’t easy for him to come to Atlanta to replace a franchise icon. But never once has there been any sort of animosity or awkwardness between the two first basemen.
In fact, the two have attended events together, including a Morgan Wallen concert at Truist Park last year. There is a genuine mutual respect.
“Matt is a great guy and an unbelievable baseball player,” Freeman said. “He's one of the best power hitters in our game right now. So it's fun. And he's from [Atlanta]. That massive home run he hit yesterday was just cool.”
Olson’s 416-foot home run in the seventh inning of Thursday’s night’s 6-2 win over the Phillies reminded the baseball world of his great power. Atlanta’s first baseman ranks fifth among all MLB players with 329 homers since the start of 2018, his first full big league season.
With the 41 homers hit this season, Olson joined Hank Aaron (eight times), Eddie Mathews (four times) and Ronald Acuña Jr. (twice) as the only players to tally multiple 40-homer seasons for the Braves.
“Matt had a lot on his plate when he first got here,” Braves manager Walt Weiss said. “He was replacing an icon. I think we got the only guy that could do it, the only guy that could step in in that role at that time. Matt's been a superstar for us.”
The Braves’ final written offer to Freeman was a five-year, $135 million deal ($27 million average annual value). The 10-time All-Star was 32 at the time.
The Braves knew Freeman might have a few more MVP-caliber seasons in him. But they also were confident Olson would provide similar production through those first few years and then continue to provide elite production while Freeman moved north of 35.
Of course, Freeman holds the edge in batting average (.306 to .259), OPS (.885 to .852) and most importantly World Series titles (2 to 0) over these past five seasons. He highlighted this run by becoming the only player in MLB history to hit a walk-off homer in a World Series game multiple times.
Olson is still bidding for that big postseason moment. But more importantly, he’s vying to lead the Braves to a World Series title, just like Freeman did in 2021.
“I’d say he’s our captain,” Braves catcher Sean Murphy said. “He goes out there every single day and hit 40 home runs. I’d say we’re happy to have Matt Olson on our team."

item.content:encoded:
Philadelphia Phillies second baseman Luis Arraez issued a statement to the team’s fans following the end of his first season with the team.
Arraez, who began the season with the San Francisco Giants, was traded to the Phillies at the MLB trade deadline as the team tried to make a deep postseason run with his bat in their lineup.
While Arraez was excellent for the Giants, he struggled a bit with the Phillies after the trade, and to make matters worse, he got injured in late September and was forced to miss the Phillies’ National League Wild Card series against the Atlanta Braves, which they lost 2-1 in a three-game set.
Still, he loved his time in Philadelphia.
Luis Arraez Issues Statement After Phillies’ Season Ends
Taking to his social media, Arraez issued a lengthy statement where he thanked the Phillies’ fans for making him feel at home for the past two months.
“Philadelphia. When I was traded to the Phillies in the middle of the season, I didn’t know what to expect. But from day one, you welcomed me with open arms and made me feel at home.Playing at Citizens Bank Park in front of a sea of red and feeling your energy is something I’ll never forget. I wanted nothing more than to finish the season on the field with my teammates. Watching the playoffs from the bench because of an injury was incredibly difficult, because all I wanted was to be out there fighting alongside them. Thank you, Phillies fans, for all your support and for making my time in Philadelphia so special. — Luis. Philadelphia,” Arraez wrote in an Instagram post.
Luis Arraez Is an Impending Free Agent
A free agent once again this winter, Arraez will be highly coveted after having an overall terrific season, one where he finished second in the NL batting title race with a .310 batting average, just one point behind the winner, Arizona Diamondbacks catcher Gabriel Moreno.
Overall, Arraez batted .310 with a .765 OPS and a 127 OPS+ on the season, though his numbers after being traded to the Phillies declined as he struggled with his new team. Even still, his final numbers for the season saw him tally a solid 2.9 bWAR.
Not only did Arraez have good overall numbers at the plate this year, but his glovework at second base also improved greatly after he was routinely criticized for his defense during the last several seasons, which included being moved to first base when he played for the San Diego Padres last year.
The Phillies will likely attempt to keep Arraez for next season and beyond, but he will likely get some very lucrative contract offers during free agency, so it’s no guarantee that he returns to the Phillies.
That being said, he obviously had a great experience playing in Philadelphia based on what he wrote in this statement, so if the team and the player’s agent can come to terms on a fair contract for both sides, then perhaps he will return to “The City of Brotherly Love” next season.

item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. – How the Yankees' Bay State duo of Cam Schlittler and Ben Rice performed in the Wild Card Series against the Red Sox – drafted out of Massachusetts – was also a take-a-bow moment for player development.
"Just impressive to see these young guys step into the biggest stage at the biggest moment,'' said Yankees captain Aaron Judge, their supreme first-round pick (32nd overall) from the 2013 draft.
Here's a look at the other Yankees drafted and developed players who could impact the best-of-five Division Series against the AL champion Tampa Bay Rays:
George Lombard Jr.
Age: 21
Yankees draft info: 1st round (26th overall) in 2023.
In his first taste of postseason – with 42 games of MLB experience – the shortstop handled his position well and went 4-for-8 at the plate.
"A couple of years ago, he was playing high school baseball,'' Judge said of Lombard, while praising the Yanks' rookie and sophomore class in general.
"Just a really good player,'' Max Fried said of Lombard Jr. "He's got a slow heartbeat.''
Spencer Jones
Age: 25
Yankees draft info: 1st round (25th overall) in 2022.
Despite Trent Grisham's return, Jones – who batted .389/1.107 OPS in 59 MLB plate appearances vs. lefties – started in center field against Payton Tolle in the Wild Card opener.
The lefty-hitting Jones was shifted to right field vs. Sonny Gray in Game 2, batting cleanup, with Grisham in center.
Jones went 2-for-8 with a walk and four strikeouts in the ALWC.
Judge's status could impact his late game at-bats, if the captain is on the roster, but the 6-foot-7 slugger has earned his opportunity as a regular in postseason.
Ben Rice
Age: 27
Yankees draft info: 12th round in 2021.
Rice destroyed the Red Sox in the Yanks' 9-0, Wild Card Series Game 1 win, with two homers - including a grand slam - among his four hits, with six RBI as the DH.
With 41 homers this year, Rice joined Judge as the only drafted Yankees to reach the 40-homer mark in a single regular season.
Expect Rice to continue batting leadoff against the Rays' right-handed starters. Also, he's a .458 hitter with five homers and a 1.685 OPS in seven career games at the Trop.
Anthony Volpe
Age: 25
Yankees draft info: 1st round (30th overall) in 2019.
Volpe started the Wild Card opener vs. the lefty Tolle, going 1-for-3 at second base, a new MLB position for him upon his return; he was optioned to Triple-A with Lombard's early August call-up.
Lefty-hitting Jazz Chisholm Jr., on the bench in WC Game 1, started Game 2 vs. the right-handed Gray and went 2-for-3 with a walk in a clinching 9-2 victory.
Given the Rays' right-handed rotation, Volpe might be a bench player this series, utilized later in games for his infield versatility (including some third base) and as a pinch-runner.
Cam Schlittler
Age: 25
Yankees draft info: 7th round in 2022.
Red Sox Nation has already seen enough postseason Schlittler, helping take Boston out of the last two AL Wild Card Series.
After his 117-pitch scoreless effort in Tuesday's Wild Card opener, Schlittler gets the ball in Monday's ALDS Game 2, on one extra day of rest.
That also puts him in line for a possible Game 5 on normal rest. Both games are at Trop, and Schlittler owns a 1.16 ERA in 17 road starts this year.
Will Warren
Age: 27
Yankees draft info: 8th round in 2021.
Moved into a multi-inning relief role in postseason, Warren tossed 1.2 innings (one run) following Fried in Game 2.
He should fit that same role against the Rays, with the ability to take over for a shaky or injured starter, or to provide a bridge to the high-leverage duo of Paul Blackburn and Brent Headrick, leading into David Bednar.
Austin Wells
Age: 27
Yankees draft info: 1st round (28th overall) in 2020.
At the plate, the lefty-hitting Wells picked it up considerably after a brutal first four months, but his value behind the plate - and his knack for ABS challenges - has been a constant.
As for defending the speedy, daring Rays, "they love to run and take advantage,'' said Wells, emphasizing the limiting of walks in this series.
Wells has been paired all year with Game 1 starter Gerrit Cole, who praised the "role Austin has played in run prevention'' for a staff that led the league in ERA.
This article originally appeared on NorthJersey.com: How these 7 Yankees homegrown players can impact ALDS vs Rays

Courtesy: TelevisaUnivision MIAMI, FL. – October 2, 2026 – TUDN Radio, the premier Hispanic sports audio network of TelevisaUnivision, will once again serve as the exclusive U.S. Spanish-language radio home for the 2026 Major League Baseball Postseason. item.content:encoded:
For the Sixth Consecutive Year, TelevisaUnivision’s Sports Audio Network Will Deliver Live, Play-by-Play Coverage of the MLB Playoffs Through the 122nd World Series Across All Platforms.
Courtesy: TelevisaUnivision
MIAMI, FL. – October 2, 2026 – TUDN Radio, the premier Hispanic sports audio network of TelevisaUnivision, will once again serve as the exclusive U.S. Spanish-language radio home for the 2026 Major League Baseball Postseason. Marking the network’s sixth consecutive edition delivering October baseball to Hispanic audiences across the nation, fans can experience the entire postseason journey entirely in Spanish—from the opening pitch of the Wild Card Series through the final out of the historic 122nd World Series.
Continuing its long-standing collaboration with Major League Baseball, TUDN Radio will bring every moment of the postseason to life, led by the voices of acclaimed announcers Luis Quiñones, Alberto “El Beto” Ferreiro, Daniel Alvarez, and Jesus Acosta. This elite broadcast team will provide unparalleled coverage across the network’s nationwide terrestrial radio footprint, as well as digitally via the Uforia app and TUDN’s digital platforms.
“Baseball holds a deep, passionate connection with our Hispanic audience, and we are incredibly proud to return for our sixth postseason as the exclusive Spanish-language audio voice of MLB,” said Carlos F. Azcarate, VP of Sports Radio Network. “We are thrilled to continue bringing fans closer to the diamond, delivering every pivotal moment, dramatic home run, and championship celebration directly to them, wherever they choose to listen.”
Unprecedented Coverage Across All Platforms
TUDN Radio will broadcast key matchups throughout each round of the postseason, culminating in comprehensive Spanish-language audio coverage of the entire Fall Classic. Listeners can tune in across multiple touchpoints:
- TUDN Radio Network: Broadcast across affiliate radio stations in primary Hispanic markets nationwide.
- The Uforia App: TelevisaUnivision’s audio platform, offering live streaming on mobile devices across the United States.
- TUDN.com and TUDN App: Live digital audio integration for fans following games online.
- Smart Speakers & Connected Devices: Voice-activated live streaming through supported home integrations.
The 2026 Postseason Schedule on TUDN Radio
TUDN Radio’s coverage will feature full pre-game, play-by-play, and post-game analysis across every round:
- MLB Wild Card Series: Complete coverage of the best-of-three opening rounds.
- American League and National League Division Series (ALDS & NLDS): In-depth coverage as teams battle for the pennant.
- American League and National League Championship Series (ALCS & NLCS): Live calls deciding the champions of each league.
- The 122nd World Series: Uninterrupted, full-series coverage of baseball’s championship showdown.
Adding to the comprehensive live game broadcasts, fans can catch all the surrounding excitement, expert breakdowns, and exclusive player interviews on TUDN Radio’s premier baseball show, Desde El Diamante.
Complete broadcast schedules, station directories, and talent assignments will be updated throughout the month as matchups advance. Fans can follow along with live game updates, highlights, and behind-the-scenes content on X, Instagram, and Facebook via @TUDNRadio and by visiting TUDN.com.
CONTACT:
Melissa Agudelo – Director of Communications, News & Sports
###

Cortesía: TelevisaUnivision
MIAMI, Florida – 2 de octubre de 2026 – TUDN Radio, la principal cadena de audio deportivo para la audiencia hispana de TelevisaUnivision, volverá a ser la casa exclusiva de radio en español en EE. UU. de la Postemporada de las Grandes Ligas 2026. Por sexto año consecutivo, la cadena llevará el beisbol de octubre a las audiencias hispanas de todo el país, permitiéndoles vivir de principio a fin la emoción de la postemporada en español, desde el primer lanzamiento de la Serie de Comodines hasta el último out de la histórica 122.ª Serie Mundial.
Como parte de su colaboración de larga trayectoria con Major League Baseball, TUDN Radio llevará a los aficionados cada instante de la postemporada de la mano de los reconocidos narradores Luis Quiñones, Alberto “El Beto” Ferreiro, Daniel Alvarez y Jesús Acosta. Este destacado equipo de transmisión ofrecerá una cobertura de primer nivel a través de la red de estaciones de radio terrestre de la cadena en todo el país, así como en formato digital mediante la app de Uforia y las plataformas digitales de TUDN.
“El beisbol mantiene un vínculo profundo y apasionado con nuestra audiencia hispana, y nos llena de orgullo regresar por sexto año consecutivo como la voz exclusiva en español de la postemporada de la MLB”, afirmó Carlos F. Azcarate, VP de Sports Radio Network. “Nos entusiasma seguir acercando a los aficionados al diamante y llevarles cada momento decisivo, cada cuadrangular dramático y cada celebración del campeonato, sin importar dónde elijan escucharnos”.
Cobertura sin precedentes en todas las plataformas
TUDN Radio transmitirá los enfrentamientos más destacados de cada ronda de la postemporada, hasta llegar a una cobertura integral en audio en español de toda la Serie Mundial. Los aficionados podrán seguir la acción a través de múltiples plataformas:
- TUDN Radio Network: Transmisiones a través de estaciones afiliadas en los principales mercados hispanos de todo el país.
- La app de Uforia: La plataforma de audio de TelevisaUnivision ofrecerá streaming en vivo para dispositivos móviles en todo Estados Unidos.
- TUDN.com y la app de TUDN: Integración de audio digital en vivo para los aficionados que sigan los partidos por internet.
- Altavoces inteligentes y dispositivos conectados: Streaming en vivo mediante comandos de voz a través de las integraciones domésticas compatibles.
Calendario de la Postemporada 2026 en TUDN Radio
La cobertura de TUDN Radio incluirá previa, narración jugada a jugada y análisis posterior a cada encuentro durante todas las rondas de la postemporada:
- Serie de Comodines de la MLB: Cobertura completa de la ronda inaugural al mejor de tres juegos.
- Series Divisionales de la Liga Americana y la Liga Nacional (ALDS y NLDS): Análisis en profundidad mientras los equipos compiten por el campeonato de cada liga.
- Series de Campeonato de la Liga Americana y la Liga Nacional (ALCS y NLCS): Narración en vivo de los encuentros que definirán a los campeones de cada liga.
- 122.ª Serie Mundial: Cobertura ininterrumpida y de principio a fin de la gran batalla por el campeonato de las Grandes Ligas.
Además de las transmisiones en vivo de los partidos, los aficionados podrán disfrutar de toda la emoción alrededor de la postemporada, análisis especializados y entrevistas exclusivas con jugadores en Desde El Diamante, el programa insignia de beisbol de TUDN Radio.
Los calendarios completos de transmisiones, directorios de estaciones y asignaciones del talento se actualizarán durante el mes a medida que avancen los enfrentamientos. Los aficionados podrán seguir las novedades de los partidos en vivo, los mejores momentos y contenido exclusivo detrás de cámaras en X, Instagram y Facebook a través de @TUDNRadio, así como en TUDN.com.

item.title: [Sportsnaut] MLB Insider Claims Phillies Will 'Kick Around Idea' of Bryce Harper Trade This Winter: 5 Potential Landing Spots, Including the NY Yankees
item.dc:creator: Jasonburgosmma; Jason Burgos
item.description: After a disappointing end to the 2026 season, a prominent MLB insider believes the Philadelphia Phillies will consider trading long-time star Bryce Harper this winter. The Phillies entered this year with the fourth-highest payroll in MLB and big expectations. item.content:encoded:
After a disappointing end to the 2026 season, a prominent MLB insider believes the Philadelphia Phillies will consider trading long-time star Bryce Harper this winter.
The Phillies entered this year with the fourth-highest payroll in MLB and big expectations. While they didn’t win the National League East, the hope was that their talent-rich roster could still go on a deep run in the postseason. Unfortunately, despite their best efforts, Philadelphia came up short in their three-game Wild Card series against division rivals the Atlanta Braves.
Following their season-ending loss on Thursday, The Athletic’s Ken Rosenthal claimed, “The Phillies at least need to kick around the idea of trading” the All-Star first baseman. A player the MLB insider feels doesn’t have an “oppressive” contract, with five years and $118 million left on the deal.
If the team pulled the trigger on a trade for the two-time NL MVP this winter, here are five teams he could end up landing with this winter.
Chicago Cubs
The Chicago Cubs had an equally frustrating finish to their 2026 campaign this week as well. However, they didn’t even get to three games, and the team with the sixth highest payroll in baseball was soundly beaten by the San Diego Padres in just two.
Chicago could lose both of their corner outfielders this winter, so Harper could fill either of those spots. Or the nine-time All-Star could be an option at DH. Either way, Harper would be a really nice addition to the lineup. Plus, like Alex Bregman, he is a strong veteran leader and player in the postseason.
Boston Red Sox
The Boston Red Sox are another team that saw their playoff run ended in just two games. In their case, it was rivals the New York Yankees who eliminated them. Harper could certainly be an option for Boston at DH. But the thing this team lacks the most, which he would address, is a proven veteran leader on the field and in the clubhouse. If he can handle the pressure of Philadelphia, Harper would be fine in Boston.
Toronto Blue Jays
This season was a massive disappointment for the Toronto Blue Jays. After being a couple of outs away from winning the World Series last fall, the Jays finished dead last in the AL East with a 79-83 record this year. So you can bet they will look to make a big move this offseason to get back into title contention in 2027.
If the Phillies actually make Harper available in trade talks, Toronto will be fascinated by the idea of pairing him with Vladimir Guerrero Jr. next season. If Guerrero Jr. can return to the player he always has been in 2027, and Kazuma Okamoto puts up similar power numbers, adding Harper to the batting order gives Toronto a spot in the order you can’t pitch around.
New York Yankees
The Yankees are still in the race to be champions in 2026. However, if they fall short of that yearly goal, the Yanks will surely look into adding a piece or two that can get them to end their 17-year title drought.
New York would need to find a new home for Giancarlo Stanton, but with only one guaranteed season for $15 million left on his deal, it may be possible this offseason. If they can trade the injury-prone five-time All-Star, a lineup with a healthy Aaron Judge, Harper, Ben Rice, and Cody Bellinger is one of the best in baseball.
St. Louis Cardinals
While the St. Louis Cardinals finished 77-85 this season, they seemed a bit ahead of schedule in their rebuild because of the upside in young stars JJ Wetherholt and Jordan Walker. The Cards are willing to make bold moves for proven stars if they feel they can help get the team to the next level or change the culture for the better. Harper could do both.
With St. Louis having a top-five farm system in MLB, they would certainly have the prospect assets to easily get a deal done.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Red Sox-Jarren Duran Outlook Just Got Much More Complicated
item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy; Unknown
item.description: The Boston Red Sox have a decision to make with outfielder Jarren Duran this offseason. item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox have a decision to make with outfielder Jarren Duran this offseason.
If you're a Red Sox fan who has been following the club over the last few years, or simply a baseball fan in general who has followed trade rumors, you've likely seen Duran's name a lot. His name was out there as a trade candidate before the 2025 season, ahead of the 2025 trade deadline, before the 2026 season and before the 2026 trade deadline. In every scenario, the Red Sox kept the speedster.
The offseason is now here for Boston and there surely will be trade chatter again with the Red Sox still having a surplus of talented outfielders. Plus, Duran just had the worst offensive season of his career to this point at the same time. The 30-year-old has two more seasons of team control beyond the 2026 season and arbitration is going to play a big role this offseason in the decision-making process. On Friday, MLB Trade Rumors released its salary estimates for arbitration-eligible players and had Duran at $11.1 million. When it comes to projecting arbitration salaries, MLB Trade Rumors is considered to be among the very best in the business.
What Should Boston Do?
Now, of course, nothing is guaranteed at this exact moment about that $11.1 million number. But if that's the direction Duran's contract is going to go, it's going to make a decision more difficult this winter. In 2026, Duran made $7.7 million and batted .207 with a .266 on-base percentage. Now, of course, his 20 homers, 69 RBIs and 21 stolen bases were good. But those batting average and on-base percentage numbers are almost unplayable.
There's no denying Duran's talent. When he's at his best, he's a five-tool player. But the 2026 season wasn't his best. In 2024, he was a 9.0 WAR player. In 2025, he was a 4.9 WAR player in what was viewed as a somewhat down year. In 2026, he was a 0.4 WAR player. It's going to be hard to argue for the increase to a number in the range that MLB Trade Rumors projected with two straight years of regression. Plus, now Duran is 30 years old.
The deadline to tender contracts is the last Friday before Thanksgiving each November. This year, that day falls on Nov. 20. If the Red Sox non-tender Duran, he would simply enter free agency. If the Red Sox tender him a contract, then that's when this number — or something similar — will come into play. For a club that needs to add more power, shelling out that much cash to Duran would be a lot. Also, a price tag that high could be difficult to trade after he just had a difficult season.
When it comes to Duran, the first decision that's going to come is tendering — or non-tendering — him. If they were to non-tender him, they save the cash but get nothing in return. It's a difficult call, to say the least.
Patrick McAvoy's experiences include local and national sports coverage at the New England Sports Network with a focus on baseball and basketball. Outside of journalism, Patrick received an MBA at Brandeis University. For all business/marketing inquiries regarding Boston Red Sox On SI, please reach out to Scott Neville: scott@moreviewsmedia.com

item.title: [PhillyVoice] This era of the Phillies feels like it's over

item.content:encoded:
October 02, 2026
Ryan Howard twisted uncomfortably out of the batter's box, then crumpled just a few steps down the first-base line as the St. Louis Cardinals rushed toward the mound to celebrate.
An October-fueled Citizens Bank Park fell silent.
The Phillies had lost Game 5 of the 2011 NLDS, and suddenly, shockingly, their all-in chase after another World Series title was over.
Roy Halladay, with his last bit of true greatness, tossed a one-run gem that should've been enough of a chance, and yet was nullified by an even more brilliant complete game from Chris Carpenter, who made a Philadelphia lineup flush with high-profile bats look entirely pedestrian.
And then there was Howard at the end, the star slugger who was left lying there in the grass as the Phillies' grand ambitions all came crashing down.
No one wanted to say it out loud at the time. Maybe they just couldn't bring themselves to fully accept it just yet. But that image has since been permanently etched into the minds of every Phillies fan who witnessed it, because deep down, everyone knew right then and there: A golden era of Phillies baseball was over.
One by one, the generation defined by Howard, Jimmy Rollins, Chase Utley, Cole Hamels, that second-ever World Championship in 2008, and then Halladay, Cliff Lee, and any other big name that the organization could get its hands on in the pursuit of one more, faded.
Those Phillies were never competitive again.
Bryce Harper whiffed on a low and way, way away slider from Chris Sale that he never had a prayer of hitting, and that Drake Baldwin, behind the plate, never had a prayer of catching.
Harper, slowly and totally unaware, bent down to take his shin guard off, thinking it was strike three and that the inning was over. He never saw the ball spike past Baldwin in the dirt, and go rolling to the backstop. By the time he realized, all he gave was a disinterested jog up the first base line, which did finally end the eighth inning from Baldwin having the time to recover for the throw up to the base.
John Kruk: "RUN!"
Bryce Harper was slow to get out of the box, not realizing strike three had gotten away.
(Via: @MLB) pic.twitter.com/GRcx3VGWtQ
— Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) October 2, 2026
The Phillies were down, 6-2, in the deciding Game 3 of the 2026 NL Wild Card series, on the road against the rival Atlanta Braves.
They still had three outs of life left, but everyone watching knew full well – and probably had no hesitation admitting this time, just shy of 15 years later – that another playoff era of Phillies baseball was over.
And once this club does get back to South Philadelphia, there will be no World Series pennant to look up at in center field and over Ashburn Alley.
The closest this generation ever got was that first breakout run that burnt out against the Astros in 2022.
They only ever got further away from it from there, and now might be all out of chances.
The Phillies stood in the visiting clubhouse, and interim manager Don Mattingly sat at the press conference dais.
No one spoke with any certainties.
Mattingly, who took over midseason for Rob Thomson, talked around whether he wanted to come back and how he felt about the decision the Phillies will have to make this winter for whoever their next full-time manager is going to be.
"It's not the time to talk about anything like that," Mattingly said. "...I want the Phillies to do what they need to do."
Granted, anything shy of a World Series always seemed to point toward him not staying.
Alec Bohm, the first-round and homegrown infielder who was good but always had better expected of him, is now headed for free agency and didn't want to talk about what his future held either.
Trea Turner, who certainly will be back just by the nature of his enormous 11-year, $300 million contract, knows he can't with another season like this one, where his numbers at the plate are low and where you can never be fully confident that he'll properly field the baseball. That can't cut it.
"[I] got a lot of work to do," Turner said.
And then there was Harper, who didn't have much to offer either, save for one definitive statement.
"I'd imagine this team's gonna look a lot different next year," said Harper, "with the guys that are kind of leaving this clubhouse. We'll see."
If there even is a next year for baseball.
Either way, it does feel like this team has to be.
The next few weeks are undoubtedly going to put the Phillies and everyone responsible for their current construction up to harsh scrutiny, amid a fan base that, really, got tired of them two postseason failures ago.
Dave Dombrowski, the Phillies' president of baseball operations, will have the most to answer for, after he repeatedly ran it back with an aging core, failed once again to put together a competent bullpen, and ended this season with none of his trade deadline acquisitions on the postseason roster, all while presiding over a barren-looking farm system.
Hitting coach Kevin Long, who has long been immune from any other shifts in the dugout staff around him, has to face the music here, too, after the Phillies continued to have a collectively abysmal approach at the plate – outside of a month – and after seeing nearly all of the Phils' batters either plateau, regress, or in the case of Luis Arráez, to see a perennial .300-plus hitter suddenly drop well below that line the second he put on a red-pinstriped uniform.
And then there's Harper, the big face of an era that kept falling short and now might not even be good enough to get there to begin with anymore.
All offseason and into spring training, it was clear he was miffed by Dombrowski openly questioning to the press last fall whether he could be "elite" anymore.
Harper said back in February that it wasn't something to motivate him, but he made it obvious, too, that those remarks stuck in his craw.
And he would go on to put up solid numbers, and yeah, he even had his heroics in a Game 2 that kept the Phillies alive for another day.
But now they're done. This era might be done, and with its end forever tied to that moment of Harper leisurely taking his shin guard off at the plate, not knowing the ball went rolling, and by the time he did, not having enough care to even try to fully run it out.
It felt a lot like Ryan Howard 15 years ago. It felt like an era was over.
This one, though, might be a bit more bitter.
*QUOTES SOURCE: NBC Sports Philadelphia on YouTube

item.dc:creator: TJ French
item.description: The Philadelphia Phillies have been eliminated from the MLB playoffs, and in case Phillies fans were not aware of it, infielder Trea Turner is just not a good defender. Phillies fans likely aren't too pleased with Turner as a whole after the NL Wild Card, as he did little with the bat and caused more harm than good with the glove in his hand. However, the bright side is there's a strong possibility Trea Turner will be removed from his duties at the shortstop position in 2027. More MLB on Heavy:
item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Phillies have been eliminated from the MLB playoffs, and in case Phillies fans were not aware of it, infielder Trea Turner is just not a good defender.
Phillies fans likely aren't too pleased with Turner as a whole after the NL Wild Card, as he did little with the bat and caused more harm than good with the glove in his hand.
However, the bright side is there's a strong possibility Trea Turner will be removed from his duties at the shortstop position in 2027.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Announce Sudden Roster Moves Before Braves Series
'Automatic' That Trea Turner Will Be Moved to Center Field
FanSided.com recently relayed the sentiment that Ken Rosenthal reported earlier today that Trea Turner will almost certainly be moved to center field in 2027:
"The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal reported on Friday that Turner moving from shortstop to center field feels like an "automatic" decision if he is not traded this offseason. The three-time All-Star is coming off a horrendous defensive season, and he topped 20 errors for the second time in four years."
Yikes… that's a lot of errors, and Trea Turner is still tied to a $300 million contract. Perhaps trading him might actually be a pretty smart idea…
Writer Jake Elman also noted why moving Turner to the outfield won't solve all the Phillies' problems:
"Change is far easier said than done, and Rosenthal acknowledged as much. Frankly, moving the two-time batting champion to the outfield is a band-aid fix at best, especially when he hasn't played outside the infield since 2016. But DHing is obviously off the table so long as Kyle Schwarber is around, and there is no indication that Turner could move to second, as he did with the Dodgers in 2021."
More MLB on Heavy: Pittsburgh Pirates Quietly Sign 7-Year MLB Player
How Bad Was Trea Turner's 2026 Season?
Trea Turner certainly held the Philadelphia Phillies backin 2026.
He batted .242 (career low) with 19 home runs, 29 doubles, and 156 hits in an MLB-leading 645 at-bats.
Turner never works walks, and he struck out 147 times, which led to another career low, posting an OPS+ of 81. Turner's career OPS+ is 116.
As far as his contract is concerned, there are still seven years left on the deal, which, if Turner's trend of struggles at the plate continues, could be a huge financial burden for Philadelphia.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Mets Trade Prediction Lands 214-Home Run Slugger

item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers have an unfortunate history of late-season injuries preceding postseason runs. September injuries to Christian Yelich and Brandon Woodruff are the most recent examples, but the trend also extends to Devin Williams breaking his hand after punching a wall in 2021, Ben Sheets not being a part of the 2008 postseason run after a flexor tendon injury, and of course, Rollie Fingers' forearm injury ahead of the team's memorable 1982 run.
With just over 24 hours remaining until the Brewers' 2026 postseason opener, this year's team thankfully hasn't made a contribution to that disheartening list. However, as the Brewers finish out their stretch of five days off -- the result of them earning a first-round bye -- there was an injury scare that had Brewers fans feeling déjà vu.
Infielder Joey Ortiz exited the Brewers' Friday night opener in their final series of the regular season with a noticeable limp. After the game, manager Pat Murphy revealed that Ortiz had been battling soreness in his knee due to a bruise he sustained during the team's series against the Philadelphia Phillies and also some inflammation in his abdomen that has been causing him discomfort.
Ortiz didn't play either of the final two games of the regular season, and his postseason roster status was briefly in doubt when Murphy couldn't commit one way or another on Tuesday afternoon. However, thankfully, during Friday's media availability, the Brewers' manager took a more optimistic tone when talking about his injured infielder. Said Murphy on Ortiz on Friday afternoon, "It looks like it's progressing in the right direction...I would say at this point we're planning on him being available."
The Brewers are planning on Joey Ortiz "being available" for the NLDS
Despite his struggles during the 2025 season and first half of the 2026 campaign, Ortiz became one of the Brewers' most productive hitters during the second half of this year. In fact, Ortiz had the ninth best OPS (.883) among NL hitters with at least 200 plate appearances, from July 1 to the end of the season. As crazy as the statement would have sounded during the middle of May, Ortiz is one of the Brewers' key offensive X-factors heading into the postseason.
Therefore, it would have been a significant blow had Ortiz missed out on the 2026 postseason run due to his late-season knee and abdomen injuries, but thankfully the Brewers' infielder is expected to be available tomorrow night.
Ortiz's production would indicate that he should start every game regardless of the handedness of the opposing pitcher, but Murphy consistently used David Hamilton against tough right-handed starters at third base, so it's not yet certain just how many games Joey O will start in the postseason. That said, the Padres just announced that southpaw Robbie Ray is getting the ball in Game 1, so Ortiz will almost certainly be manning the hot corner on Saturday night. Regardless of how many at-bats Murphy gives his surging third baseman in October, it's undeniably a welcome development that Ortiz will likely be available for the NLDS roster.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Phillies' Trea Turner Gets Honest About Switching Positions After Tough Year
item.dc:creator: Matt Levine
item.description: After a tough end to the 2026 MLB season, the Philadelphia Phillies are now entering a crucial offseason that will be filled with all sorts of questions. Many of these will be centered around who the next manager will be, with interim skipper Don Mattingly not expected to return. But there are plenty of others that could determine the fate of the Phillies moving forward. One of which has to do with star shortstop Trea Turner, following a rough year for the veteran. The 33 year old played in 157
item.content:encoded:
After a tough end to the 2026 MLB season, the Philadelphia Phillies are now entering a crucial offseason that will be filled with all sorts of questions.
Many of these will be centered around who the next manager will be, with interim skipper Don Mattingly not expected to return. But there are plenty of others that could determine the fate of the Phillies moving forward.
One of which has to do with star shortstop Trea Turner, following a rough year for the veteran. The 33 year old played in 157 games for Philadelphia this year, and he saw issues take place both at the plate and defensively.
Offensively, Turner hit .242 with 19 home runs and 58 RBIs, while posting an OPS of .675. Statistically, 2026 was the worst of his career since his rookie year, and his issues really held this team back.
But entering the offseason, there are real questions around whether Turner can remain at shortstop. When the Phillies signed him a few years ago, the idea was to have him be the shortstop for the rest of his career, but other teams were wary about his long-term ability to play the position.
Now, Philadelphia is weighing how to proceed with the veteran infielder, and changes could be made as early as next season. When asked about the possibility of making a position change next year, Turner wouldn't commit to anything, saying that he would see what happens over the offseason.
But the veteran did say that he understands questions will be asked after the year that he just put together. The Phillies' offseason will be centered around multiple decisions, with this being one of the biggest for the team.
Once Philadelphia finds its new manager, this could be an early conversation that will need to be had. Turner still has seven more years left on his massive contract that he signed with the Phillies, so whoever takes over will need to do this carefully.
The veteran has declined fairly heavily at shortstop, and he is now viewed as a liability at the position. So, while the new manager will tread carefully with Turner, it's a move that will need to be made.
Nothing is guaranteed of course, and Turner could remain as the team's shortstop next season. But for this team to reach the heights that they want to get too, this is certainly a decision that needs to be discussed heavily as the winter starts.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Joey Ortiz Injury Update for NLDS Game 1 (Everything Brewers Fans Need to Know)
item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers don't have to reveal their National League Division Series roster until Saturday morning, but the organization gave a positive update on Friday ahead of the official announcement. Throughout the week, the guy to watch from an injury perspective has been infielder Joey Ortiz. item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers don't have to reveal their National League Division Series roster until Saturday morning, but the organization gave a positive update on Friday ahead of the official announcement.
Throughout the week, the guy to watch from an injury perspective has been infielder Joey Ortiz. The 28-year-old has been dealing with knee and abdominal injuries, but is trending in the right direction. Brewers manager Pat Murphy said so himself on Friday and noted that the expectation is that he will be good to go for the National League Division Series.
"It looks like it's progressing in the right direction," Murphy said. "He's still ... he still has some pain. He's going to tell you, 'no,' and all that kind of stuff. He wants to play very badly. I would say at this point, we are planning on him being available."
Joey Ortiz Is Going To Be Alright
There was a point during the 2026 season in which this update wouldn't have moved the needle much for Milwaukee. But things are certainly different now. Before he shifted from shortstop to third base, Ortiz was really struggling offensively. He was batting .207 with one home run and 14 RBIs in 60 games before Cooper Pratt made his big league debut. Pratt made his debut on June 16, which shifted Ortiz's role away from shortstop.
Things changed for the better for Ortiz afterward. From June 17 through the end of the season, Ortiz slashed .310/.348/.491 with an .840 OPS, eight home runs, 33 RBIs, nine doubles and four triples in 74 games.
He went from being someone at risk of being sent down to the minors, to being integral to this club's success down the stretch. Fortunately, when the Brewers open up National League Division Series play on Saturday, the current expectation is that Ortiz will be in the mix, barring some sort of last-second setback.
The Brewers have a tough series ahead. The San Diego Padres are the hottest team in baseball and aren't going to be an easy out. For the Brewers to win, they're going to need all of the help that they can get. So, this update is very positive for the organization heading into their most important series of the season so far. If the Brewers can take down the Padres in the NLDS, they would advance to face either the Los Angeles Dodgers or the Atlanta Braves in the National League Championship Series.
Patrick McAvoy's experiences include local and national sports coverage at the New England Sports Network with a focus on baseball and basketball. Outside of journalism, Patrick received an MBA at Brandeis University. For all business/marketing inquiries regarding "Milwaukee Brewers On SI," please reach out to Scott Neville: scott@moreviewsmedia.com

item.title: [MLB.com] Here's how the pitching might line up for the White Sox-Guardians ALDS
item.dc:creator: Tim Stebbins; Scott Merkin
item.description: CLEVELAND -- While battling for the American League Central title last month, the Guardians and White Sox divisional race featured an added reward: a first-round bye in the postseason that would allow the champ to set its preferred pitching plan for the AL Division Series. That’s where we find ourselves now, as Cleveland and Chicago get set for their first-ever playoff matchup. As the AL Central champion Guardians enjoyed a bye this week, they also lined up their staff anchors for the first two
item.content:encoded:
CLEVELAND -- While battling for the American League Central title last month, the Guardians and White Sox divisional race featured an added reward: a first-round bye in the postseason that would allow the champ to set its preferred pitching plan for the AL Division Series.
That’s where we find ourselves now, as Cleveland and Chicago get set for their first-ever playoff matchup.
As the AL Central champion Guardians enjoyed a bye this week, they also lined up their staff anchors for the first two games of ALDS, which is set to kick off with Game 1 on Saturday at Progressive Field. Meanwhile, the White Sox are working through things after they completed a sweep of the Astros in the best-of-three AL Wild Card Series on Wednesday to advance.
Chicago’s plan, understandably, is less settled coming off its Wild Card series, though Cleveland has some uncertainty as well. What could the pitching matchups look like? Let’s take a look.
Guardians
Messick has come a long way in one year. The lefty wasn’t on the Guardians’ roster in the 2025 AL Wild Card Series, following his seven-start debut stint in the Majors down the stretch. This spring, he had to earn a spot on Cleveland’s Opening Day roster. Now, the Guards are hoping he paves the way as they push for October glory.
Messick’s stellar rookie season could make him a finalist for both the AL Cy Young Award and the Rookie of the Year Award. The 25-year-old had a 2.56 ERA (seventh in MLB) in 186 1/3 innings over 32 starts, with 193 strikeouts and 49 walks. In perhaps a good omen, he was particularly effective against Chicago, logging a 2.81 ERA with 29 strikeouts and five walks in 25 2/3 innings over four starts.
If you like pitchers with overpowering stuff, Game 2 could be appointment viewing. This season, Williams racked up 248 strikeouts (second in MLB to Jacob Misiorowski’s 252) in 184 1/3 innings over 32 starts, all of which were career highs. He had double-digit punchouts in 11 of those outings, which led the Majors.
None of those 11 starts were against Chicago, though Williams did record a 3.98 ERA with 28 strikeouts and eight walks in 20 1/3 innings over four starts against the White Sox. His Game 2 assignment is noteworthy because it lines him up to pitch Game 5 (if necessary) back in Cleveland, whereas Messick is lined up for Game 4 in Chicago. Williams had a 2.84 ERA in 18 home starts this season, and a 5.05 ERA in 14 road starts.
The Guardians are still working through their plan here. Manager Stephen Vogt noted Thursday that they want to see how Games 1 and 2 go and what their potential needs are before making a decision.
Why could it be Espino? Of the 14 position players on the White Sox Wild Card Series roster, there were six lefties and one switch-hitter. Starting Espino as an opener for lefty Joey Cantillo could force Chicago to make a lineup decision, such as whether to start lefty smasher Randal Grichuk against Espino, or call his number after Cantillo enters.
Espino served as an opener in Cantillo’s final three appearances of the regular season after the lefty encountered some command issues. Cantillo tossed 15 scoreless innings, allowing five hits and four walks, while striking out 17 batters in those outings. The formula could work in October.
All that being said: The Guardians have a flurry of options, between Espino/Cantillo, Tanner Bibee and Foster Griffin. Stay tuned.
White Sox
Some of the TBDs in terms of White Sox starters were cleared up on Friday by manager Will Venable. It begins with Smith, the rookie southpaw, who gets the same Game 1 honor as he did in the sweep of Houston during the AL Wild Card Series.
“They're a really good team. This will be my third time playing [them] since I got up here,” Smith said Friday. “So just kind of familiar with the guys and their lineup and familiar with the scouting reports against them. We are both good teams. We play hard. They play hard. So it's going to be a good series.“
With Sunday’s off-day, Burke would be pitching on regular rest Monday after striking out eight over four innings against the Astros on Wednesday. Venable confirmed Friday that Burke will pitch on Monday and will not pitch on Saturday, but the skipper did not confirm if it would be as a starter or bulk hurler.
Burke recently joked that the White Sox have 13 pitchers, or 12 in the Wild Card round, but they don’t look at anyone as a starter or reliever. This is not a situation of trying to outsmart the opposition by usage of an opener, but it’s more about Venable and his staff trying to win each game and nothing more. It has produced one of the best Major League Baseball stories this season, so why change now?
Again, Kay would make sense, having last pitched Wednesday. But he might be needed in one of the first two games. Everything is fluid.
One thing to consider: Davis Martin has a 5-3 record with a 3.13 ERA over 15 home starts against a 4-5 record and 4.68 ERA over 14 appearances (13 starts) on the road. Let’s not forget rookie Noah Schultz, who has been impressive working multiple innings out of the bullpen, or rookie David Sandlin, a starter who worked in relief against the Astros. Sean Newcomb has done a little bit of everything this season, with a 3.24 ERA over eight games against the Guardians. So he’s always a possibility.
Don’t overlook Smith coming back, with Venable discussing Smith and Taylor potentially being available for all three games.

The Atlanta Braves have been meticulous in how they handle Chris Sale for the last three years, making sure to give him enough rest so that he can maintain his excellent form for an entire campaign. The 2024 National League Cy Young Award winner has still spent time on the injured list, but their plan has helped him become a top-tier starting pitcher
item.content:encoded:
Braves' Walt Weiss provides update on Chris Sale NLDS plan appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Atlanta Braves have been meticulous in how they handle Chris Sale for the last three years, making sure to give him enough rest so that he can maintain his excellent form for an entire campaign. The 2024 National League Cy Young Award winner has still spent time on the injured list, but their plan has helped him become a top-tier starting pitcher once again. All bets are off in the playoffs, though. Right?
Two days after starting Game 1 of the NL Wild Card Series versus the Philadelphia Phillies, Sale made it clear he wanted to take the mound in a do-or-die Game 3. Despite holding a 6-2 lead in the eighth inning, manager Walt Weiss brought in the veteran left-hander to finish off Atlanta's longtime rival. Sale indicated that he still plans to pitch against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Sunday night, but nothing is official yet.
In fact, it sounds like there is serious doubt surrounding the 10-time All-Star's status for Game 2 of the NL Division Series. Although Weiss said a Sale start in LA is "still on the table," the Braves want their ace to be fresh enough for postseason battle.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
"We're gonna err on the side of giving him (time to rest) if it's even close," the NL Manager of the Year candidate revealed, per ESPN's Alden Gonzalez. That statement is a far cry from Sale's confident remarks following Atlanta's series-clinching win over Philly. Weiss has been in baseball a long time, however.
It is possible the skipper is just engaging in some good old-fashioned gamesmanship before his squad faces the two-time reigning World Series champions. The Braves are a title contender in their own right, but they will want to gain a mental edge on the Dodgers if one is attainable. Disarming the home team with a surprise pitching move seems like the perfect gambit to try in October. Dave Roberts is a veteran of this game as well, though, so he may not be caught off guard.
Of course, there is a possibility that Walt Weiss is merely telling the truth. Perhaps Atlanta will wait until it returns to Truist Park to start Chris Sale. If so, then the team's bullpen move in Game 3 of the Wild Card round will seem even more puzzling.
One thing is for certain. Sale is a warrior who has openly expressed his desire to carry a big workload in the playoffs. We shall see if the Braves trust him to run wild in Chavez Ravine. The time for speculation will soon end. Game 1 of the NLDS begins on Saturday at 4 p.m. ET.

"I think this year is the bigge
item.content:encoded:
Phillies fans responded to shortstop Trea Turner's comments about his offensive performance during the postgame interview following Philadelphia's early postseason exit on Thursday. The Phillies lost the deciding game of the NLWCS to the Braves on Thursday, failing to advance to the NLDS.
In an interview clip shared by NBC Philadelphia's John Clark, Turner admitted to a poor season at the plate and said he had to find answers to his struggles during the offseason. "I think this year is the biggest question mark for me offensively in a long time. I've got a lot of work to do," Turner said about his 2026 offensive woes.
Watch the video here:
Philadelphia fans were quick to notice Turner's comments in the postgame interview. They slammed the shortstop for his hesitant response to the question, sharing their blunt reactions on social media.
"300 mil of work to do. Go to another team, thanks," one fan commented.
Many fans fired shots at Turner by recalling his massive 11-year, $300 million contract, which he signed with the team during the 2022 offseason. The contract officially runs until 2033, and that has made multiple fans concerned about his form at the plate in the past few years.
Trea Turner Produced Disappointing Numbers at the Plate in 2026
Overall, Turner finished the regular season with a .242 batting average, 19 home runs, 58 RBIs, and a .675 OPS. These numbers are comparable to those from his rookie season with the Washington Nationals in 2015.
The Phillies invested heavily in the shortstop, who has a strong track record on both offense and defense. However, he has not yet realized his full potential for the team and its dedicated fans.
In the three NLWCS games against Atlanta, Turner managed only one hit, scoring one run and recording one RBI, stats that fall short of expectations for a star slugger in such important playoff matchups.
However, the three-time All-Star and 2019 World Series champion now has a lot to figure out during the offseason to come back stronger next year.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers postseason primer: Where do Shohei Ohtani and everyone else stand as they go for a three-peat?
item.dc:creator: Jack Baer
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers' quest for a three-peat begins in earnest on Saturday with Game 1 of the NLDS, as they seek to become the first time since the 1998-2000 New York Yankees to complete a trilogy of titles. Up to this point, the path for L.A. hasn't been entirely straightforward.
